nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a finite set of primes and let $k$ be the number of elements of $P$. Then there is an injective sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots$ of primes such that $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ are exactly the elements of $P$, every prime occurs in the sequence, and for every $n \ge k$ there is a set $I \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $a_n$ divides
nodes.title: Some generalized Euclid sequence contains every prime

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $x$, $\rho$ and $n$, the multiple-counting Jacobsthal sequence $J_{x,\rho}(n)$ is the number of multiples of $\rho$ strictly between $x^n$ and $x^{n+1}$, that is, the number of natural numbers $k$ with $x^n < k < x^{n+1}$ and $\rho \mid k$.
nodes.title: Multiple-counting Jacobsthal sequence

nodes.summary: The odd Lichtenberg numbers form the sequence $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of natural numbers defined by $a_0 = 1$ and $a_{n+1} = 4 a_n + 1$, so the sequence begins $1, 5, 21, 85, \dots$; these are the positive terms of OEIS A002450.
